sentences.d: The Ludwig Museum’s collection, which has been developing and expanding for several decades, features a number of contemporary works that deal with imaginary visions of the future or interpret the present as a dystopian reflection of the past in some way.
sentences.s: The Ludwig Museum’s collection, which has been developing and expanding for several decades, features a number of contemporary works that deal with imaginary visions of the future or interpret the present as a dystopian reflection of the past in some way.

sentences.d: These are artistic thought experiments that paint a dark picture of the possible future or present, connecting the current and the future in time, offering a glimpse into the future of humanity.
sentences.s: These are artistic thought experiments that paint a dark picture of the possible future or present, connecting the current and the future in time, offering a glimpse into the future of humanity.

sentences.d: The dystopian idea, as one of the extreme values of possible realities, is also a model, a point of reference, the contemplation of which is natural and necessary for understanding actual reality, and in this sense it is both a tool and a method.
sentences.s: The dystopian idea, as one of the extreme values of possible realities, is also a model, a point of reference, the contemplation of which is natural and necessary for understanding actual reality, and in this sense it is both a tool and a method.

sentences.d: As the first stage of a longer-term research project, the exhibition examines the works in the collection through the concept of dystopia and includes other works by artists featured in the collection in this exploration.
sentences.s: As the first stage of a longer-term research project, the exhibition examines the works in the collection through the concept of dystopia and includes other works by artists featured in the collection in this exploration.

sentences.d: The selected works represent the discourse that has been taking place recently, primarily in the Hungarian art scene, which the exhibition analyzes along various thematic paths.
sentences.s: The selected works represent the discourse that has been taking place recently, primarily in the Hungarian art scene, which the exhibition analyzes along various thematic paths.

sentences.d: This phase serves as a preparatory stage for a broader inquiry, laying the groundwork for a more comprehensive analysis of our present, current interpretations of the concept of dystopia, and contemporary artistic visions of the future.

sentences.d: Dystopia is a fictional representation of the world that presents negative developments in the present or future, usually through totalitarian, technocratic, or dehumanising structures.
sentences.s: Dystopia is a fictional representation of the world that presents negative developments in the present or future, usually through totalitarian, technocratic, or dehumanising structures.

sentences.d: The central element of the dystopian worldview is social oppression, which involves control mechanisms at the collective level and limited freedom, loss of identity, and moral dilemmas at the individual level.
sentences.s: The central element of the dystopian worldview is social oppression, which involves control mechanisms at the collective level and limited freedom, loss of identity, and moral dilemmas at the individual level.

sentences.d: The concept of dystopia, which can be interpreted as a separate category in the history of ideas, is usually defined in relation to utopia (anti-utopia), but it is also subject to strong conceptual relativism.
sentences.s: The concept of dystopia, which can be interpreted as a separate category in the history of ideas, is usually defined in relation to utopia (anti-utopia), but it is also subject to strong conceptual relativism.

sentences.d: In contrast to utopia, which is the guiding idea of an ideal society, dystopia describes a radically opposite world, where the fictional world is always worse than the existing one.
sentences.s: In contrast to utopia, which is the guiding idea of an ideal society, dystopia describes a radically opposite world, where the fictional world is always worse than the existing one.

sentences.d: Dystopia as anti-utopia serves primarily as a (dark) mirror: the conditions and characteristics of the world it depicts amplify the negative aspects of the observer’s world.
sentences.s: Dystopia as anti-utopia serves primarily as a (dark) mirror: the conditions and characteristics of the world it depicts amplify the negative aspects of the observer’s world.

sentences.d: By magnifying our inner fears, it helps us understand what kind of future we want to avoid.
sentences.s: By magnifying our inner fears, it helps us understand what kind of future we want to avoid.

sentences.d: Dystopia thus offers a radical critique of current social trends, a conceptual mapping of the crisis symptoms of modernity, which is also a source of anxiety.
sentences.s: Dystopia thus offers a radical critique of current social trends, a conceptual mapping of the crisis symptoms of modernity, which is also a source of anxiety.

sentences.d: A. The Sadness of Fulfilled Tales
sentences.s: Section A. The Sadness of Fulfilled Tales.

sentences.d: In today’s post-utopian world, the dream of a better future that once loomed on the horizon seems to have evaporated.
sentences.s: In today’s post-utopian world, the dream of a better future that once loomed on the horizon seems to have evaporated.

sentences.d: In literature and film, the genre of science fiction made huge strides in the last decades of the 20th century, permeating everyday life, not least thanks to the achievements of the scientific and technological revolution.
sentences.s: In literature and film, the genre of science fiction made huge strides in the last decades of the twentieth century, permeating everyday life, not least thanks to the achievements of the scientific and technological revolution.

sentences.d: Within this genre, dystopia, whether as anti-utopia or negative utopia, has clearly earned a place for itself.
sentences.s: Within this genre, dystopia, whether as anti-utopia or negative utopia, has clearly earned a place for itself.

sentences.d: In Hungary, the Kozmosz Fantasztikus Könyvek (Cosmos Fantastic Books) series sought to bring the sci-fi genre, which was otherwise labelled as children’s literature by the socialist party leadership and therefore considered frivolous, into the mainstream.
sentences.s: In Hungary, the Kozmos Fontostikush Kunyvek (Cosmos Fantastic Books) series sought to bring the sci-fi genre, which was otherwise labelled as children’s literature by the socialist party leadership and therefore considered frivolous, into the mainstream.

sentences.d: This is how, a few years after their publication in their original language, numerous works from a wide spectrum of world literature were translated, which, in a closed socialist system, were a real intellectual nourishment for the construction of unique worlds or even escapism, not least thanks to the high quality of the translations.
sentences.s: This is how, a few years after their publication in their original language, numerous works from a wide spectrum of world literature were translated, which, in a closed socialist system, were a real intellectual nourishment for the construction of unique worlds or even escapism, not least thanks to the high quality of the translations.

sentences.d: The section entitled The Sadness of Fulfilled Tales is like a time loop in which the present, past, and future converge—as if the present were a black mirror reflecting an entirely non-fictional image of the future for the past.
sentences.s: The section entitled The Sadness of Fulfilled Tales is like a time loop in which the present, past, and future converge, as if the present were a black mirror reflecting an entirely non-fictional image of the future for the past.

sentences.d: The exponentially accelerated scientific and technological developments that are changing our present at an unparalleled pace, coupled with the transformation of economic systems and processes, create an intriguing situation in light of the vivid dystopias that have emerged in recent decades: looking into it, our present appears to be a black mirror of the past, depicting oppressive premonitions and bad scenarios as reality rather than fiction.
sentences.s: The exponentially accelerated scientific and technological developments that are changing our present at an unparalleled pace, coupled with the transformation of economic systems and processes, create an intriguing situation in light of the vivid dystopias that have emerged in recent decades: looking into it, our present appears to be a black mirror of the past, depicting oppressive premonitions and bad scenarios as reality rather than fiction.

sentences.d: The concrete political manifestations of dystopia generate grim realisations: have we always lived in a dystopia?
sentences.s: The concrete political manifestations of dystopia generate grim realisations: have we always lived in a dystopia?

sentences.d: Further questions: does every dystopia start out as a utopia and inevitably end as an anti-utopia?
sentences.s: Further questions: does every dystopia start out as a utopia and inevitably end as an anti-utopia?

sentences.d: Are dystopias proof of the impossibility of utopias, or are we talking about two fundamentally different worlds?
sentences.s: Are dystopias proof of the impossibility of utopias, or are we talking about two fundamentally different worlds?

sentences.d: This thematic section bears the melancholy of the day after.
sentences.s: This thematic section bears the melancholy of the day after.

sentences.d: It is the bittersweet recognition that the grand narratives have come to an end, or at least that we cannot find the way to them.
sentences.s: It is the bittersweet recognition that the grand narratives have come to an end, or at least that we cannot find the way to them.

sentences.d: Behind the concepts and their signifiers, instructive works and practices appear in the section: they document how dynamics may emerge in the background that result in a world conceived as utopian turning into a dystopia in reality, just as the past, turning towards the future, surrenders to the present.
sentences.s: Behind the concepts and their signifiers, instructive works and practices appear in the section: they document how dynamics may emerge in the background that result in a world conceived as utopian turning into a dystopia in reality, just as the past, turning towards the future, surrenders to the present.

sentences.d: B. Personal Worlds
sentences.s: Section B. Personal Worlds.

sentences.d: Dystopia is traditionally an imaginary reflection of our collective fears and social anxieties: imagined futures that anticipate the conflicts of the present.
sentences.s: Dystopia is traditionally an imaginary reflection of our collective fears and social anxieties: imagined futures that anticipate the conflicts of the present.

sentences.d: In this section, the emphasis shifts: grand narratives are replaced by individual perspectives, personal visions of the future, and the inner space of the creative self.
sentences.s: In this section, the emphasis shifts: grand narratives are replaced by individual perspectives, personal visions of the future, and the inner space of the creative self.

sentences.d: The works on display do not outline a single, universal outcome, but rather a variety of possible futures existing in parallel—each through the perspective of a single creative consciousness.
sentences.s: The works on display do not outline a single, universal outcome, but rather a variety of possible futures existing in parallel, each through the perspective of a single creative consciousness.

sentences.d: Personal Worlds brings together contemporary artworks that explore utopias and dystopias in which creators build worlds from their personal experiences, intuitions, and doubts.
sentences.s: Personal Worlds brings together contemporary artworks that explore utopias and dystopias in which creators build worlds from their personal experiences, intuitions, and doubts.

sentences.d: These visions of the future are often fragmented, uncertain, and open-ended: they raise questions about social coexistence, the role of technology, the environmental crisis, and the transformation of identity, while not ruling out the possibility of individual responsibility and action.
sentences.s: These visions of the future are often fragmented, uncertain, and open-ended: they raise questions about social coexistence, the role of technology, the environmental crisis, and the transformation of identity, while not ruling out the possibility of individual responsibility and action.

sentences.d: In the works presented, global issues—climate change, social inequalities, surveillance/inspection, alienation—are closely intertwined with the position of the individual.
sentences.s: In the works presented, global issues, climate change, social inequalities, surveillance, inspection, alienation, are closely intertwined with the position of the individual.

sentences.d: The self appears in these futures sometimes as an observer, sometimes as a victim, and sometimes as an active agent.
sentences.s: The self appears in these futures sometimes as an observer, sometimes as a victim, and sometimes as an active agent.

sentences.d: The artists do not view dystopia from the outside: they live in it, are part of it, shape it, or suffer from it.
sentences.s: The artists do not view dystopia from the outside: they live in it, are part of it, shape it, or suffer from it.

sentences.d: The emphasis on personal position shifts dystopia from mere warning toward self-reflection.
sentences.s: The emphasis on personal position shifts dystopia from mere warning toward self-reflection.

sentences.d: These works do not offer exclusively dark visions.
sentences.s: These works do not offer exclusively dark visions.

sentences.d: In many cases, they also suggest alternatives, transitional states, fragile utopias—possible escape routes, new forms of coexistence, concrete tools and practices, personal strategies for survival or resistance.
sentences.s: In many cases, they also suggest alternatives, transitional states, fragile utopias, possible escape routes, new forms of coexistence, concrete tools and practices, personal strategies for survival or resistance.

sentences.d: In the works of Personal Worlds, the situations and characters that appear alongside dystopian visions do not necessarily offer the promise of a sure solution, but rather maintain the idea of possibility: the chance that the future/present is not just a series of inevitable outcomes, but a shared space that can be constantly renegotiated and rewritten.
sentences.s: In the works of Personal Worlds, the situations and characters that appear alongside dystopian visions do not necessarily offer the promise of a sure solution, but rather maintain the idea of possibility: the chance that the future, present is not just a series of inevitable outcomes, but a shared space that can be constantly renegotiated and rewritten.

sentences.d: Through contemporary visual art, Personal Worlds thus examines the role of individual responsibility, imagination, and decision-making in the process of constituting the future.
sentences.s: Through contemporary visual art, Personal Worlds thus examines the role of individual responsibility, imagination, and decision-making in the process of constituting the future.

sentences.d: C. The End of Ideology
sentences.s: Section C. The End of Ideology.

sentences.d: Ideology (a set of beliefs, social consciousness): a system of coherent ideas, views, values, and concepts professed by a given social group (class, party, stratum) that describes and interprets the world (worldview) and formulates goals and operating principles for society, justifying or criticising the existing power relations.
sentences.s: Ideology (a set of beliefs, social consciousness): a system of coherent ideas, views, values, and concepts professed by a given social group (class, party, stratum) that describes and interprets the world (worldview) and formulates goals and operating principles for society, justifying or criticising the existing power relations.

sentences.d: The first half of the 20th century was not only fifty-years of dictatorships, but also the heyday of militant ideologies.
sentences.s: The first half of the twentieth century was not only fifty-years of dictatorships, but also the heyday of militant ideologies.

sentences.d: Although utopia and dystopia are genres originating in literature, they are nevertheless ideas relating to the organisation of human society.
sentences.s: Although utopia and dystopia are genres originating in literature, they are nevertheless ideas relating to the organisation of human society.

sentences.d: Our historical experience shows that dystopia is not the realm of speculative fiction, but a very tangible everyday reality.
sentences.s: Our historical experience shows that dystopia is not the realm of speculative fiction, but a very tangible everyday reality.

sentences.d: In the wake of the past, the future has also become uncertain, with at least the looming threat of a dehumanized world.
sentences.s: In the wake of the past, the future has also become uncertain, with at least the looming threat of a dehumanized world.

sentences.d: The term the end of ideology comes from Daniel Bell’s 1960 essay of the same name.
sentences.s: The term the end of ideology comes from Daniel Bell’s 1960 essay of the same name.

sentences.d: According to the author, the great ideologies of the 20th century (communism, fascism, liberalism, conservatism, etc.) are weakening, losing their appeal, and being replaced by pragmatism, postmodern relativism, populism, technocracy, and everyday, non-ideological political actions and identity politics, resulting in a more confusing and less transparent political world.
sentences.s: According to the author, the great ideologies of the twentieth century (communism, fascism, liberalism, conservatism, etc.) are weakening, losing their appeal, and being replaced by pragmatism, postmodern relativism, populism, technocracy, and everyday, non-ideological political actions and identity politics, resulting in a more confusing and less transparent political world.

sentences.d: The collapse of large-scale, comprehensive ideological systems is due, on the one hand, to the negative aspects of their implementation (socialism, capitalism) (utopia – dystopia) and, on the other hand, to the unforeseeable effects of social change.
sentences.s: The collapse of large-scale, comprehensive ideological systems is due, on the one hand, to the negative aspects of their implementation (socialism, capitalism) (utopia to dystopia) and, on the other hand, to the unforeseeable effects of social change.

sentences.d: The end of ideologies can first be recognized by its symptoms of crisis: the loss of grand narratives, the inability of a given ideology to comprehensively describe and interpret the functioning, motivations, and goals of society or its individual parts.
sentences.s: The end of ideologies can first be recognized by its symptoms of crisis: the loss of grand narratives, the inability of a given ideology to comprehensively describe and interpret the functioning, motivations, and goals of society or its individual parts.

sentences.d: The end of ideologies can also be understood as the dystopian realisation of social utopias (ideologies) that once set out to improve the world.
sentences.s: The end of ideologies can also be understood as the dystopian realisation of social utopias (ideologies) that once set out to improve the world.

sentences.d: In this region of Europe, we may have plenty of personal or historical experience of the dominance of ideologies and their sudden collapse.
sentences.s: In this region of Europe, we may have plenty of personal or historical experience of the dominance of ideologies and their sudden collapse.

sentences.d: The period closest to us in time, permeated by ideology, is the decades of socialism, which defined a phase in the lives of many artists.
sentences.s: The period closest to us in time, permeated by ideology, is the decades of socialism, which defined a phase in the lives of many artists.

sentences.d: Consequently, a significant number of works in the museum’s collection and in the exhibition focus on the issue of the recent decline of ideology (communism/socialism, Marxism, dialectical materialism...) and its lifeworld.
sentences.s: Consequently, a significant number of works in the museum’s collection and in the exhibition focus on the issue of the recent decline of ideology (communism, socialism, Marxism, dialectical materialism..) and its lifeworld.

sentences.d: The works examine the ideologies of the era from different perspectives, mostly interpreting them beyond the framework of memory.
sentences.s: The works examine the ideologies of the era from different perspectives, mostly interpreting them beyond the framework of memory.

sentences.d: Evoking symbols of the past and empty signs, they examine the validity of ideologies, their past and their possible future.
sentences.s: Evoking symbols of the past and empty signs, they examine the validity of ideologies, their past and their possible future.

sentences.d: D. No(n) Future!
sentences.s: Section D. No(n) Future!.

sentences.d: French anthropologist Marc Augé captured one of the fundamental experiences of space use in late modern societies with his concept of non-places (non-lieux).
sentences.s: French anthropologist Mark Oh-zhay captured one of the fundamental experiences of space use in late modern societies with his concept of non-places (non-lee-uh).

sentences.d: According to his definition, non-places are spaces that have no identity-based, historical, or relational significance: they are transitory, functional, and impersonal.
sentences.s: According to his definition, non-places are spaces that have no identity-based, historical, or relational significance: they are transitory, functional, and impersonal.

sentences.d: As spaces of transportation, consumption, and administration, they are pivotal locations of everyday life, yet they lack everything that makes a ‘place’ meaningful in Augé’s interpretation.
sentences.s: As spaces of transportation, consumption, and administration, they are pivotal locations of everyday life, yet they lack everything that makes a ‘place’ meaningful in Augé’s interpretation.

sentences.d: They convey a sense of alienation, anonymity, and timelessness, while being fundamental infrastructural elements of the functioning of global society.
sentences.s: They convey a sense of alienation, anonymity, and timelessness, while being fundamental infrastructural elements of the functioning of global society.

sentences.d: The works in this section examine the concepts of place and non-place in the context of dystopia.
sentences.s: The works in this section examine the concepts of place and non-place in the context of dystopia.

sentences.d: The dystopian potential of non-places lies in the fact that, as the antithesis of places, they are social tropes of alienation, homelessness, surveillance, observation, and discomfort.
sentences.s: The dystopian potential of non-places lies in the fact that, as the antithesis of places, they are social tropes of alienation, homelessness, surveillance, observation, and discomfort.

sentences.d: The presence of the individual in these spaces is temporary and regulated: movement is controlled, identity is reduced, behaviour is prescribed.
sentences.s: The presence of the individual in these spaces is temporary and regulated: movement is controlled, identity is reduced, behaviour is prescribed.

sentences.d: The works often reinforce this state, shifting non-places toward total spaces of the future, where personal memory and attachment are permanently dissolved in the logic of function and system.
sentences.s: The works often reinforce this state, shifting non-places toward total spaces of the future, where personal memory and attachment are permanently dissolved in the logic of function and system.

sentences.d: At the same time, the No(n) Future! section does not exclusively convey the narrative of loss.
sentences.s: At the same time, the No(n) Future! section does not exclusively convey the narrative of loss.

sentences.d: Several works also question whether non-places are truly devoid of meaning or whether they simply offer different types of experiences.
sentences.s: Several works also question whether non-places are truly devoid of meaning or whether they simply offer different types of experiences.

sentences.d: There are works that attempt to reinterpret, appropriate, and transform non-places into temporary ‘places,’ raising the question of whether it is possible to create personal or collective meaning in late modern spatial structures.
sentences.s: There are works that attempt to reinterpret, appropriate, and transform non-places into temporary ‘places,’ raising the question of whether it is possible to create personal or collective meaning in late modern spatial structures.

sentences.d: They approach the exploration of dystopian non-places and the presentation of their characteristics from the perspective of public space, memory, and cultural topology.
sentences.s: They approach the exploration of dystopian non-places and the presentation of their characteristics from the perspective of public space, memory, and cultural topology.

sentences.d: The works in this section thus offer a critical examination of the spatial experience of the future.
sentences.s: The works in this section thus offer a critical examination of the spatial experience of the future.

sentences.d: Dystopia here is not necessarily a distant, imagined world, but an exaggerated, radicalized version of the spaces of the present.
sentences.s: Dystopia here is not necessarily a distant, imagined world, but an exaggerated, radicalized version of the spaces of the present.
